papers.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and Extrapolating the Capabilities of Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces BIG-bench, a collaborative benchmark with 204 tasks including moral reasoning, tested across multiple language models. Reveals scaling patterns and capability gaps in LLMs.

papers.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Presents HELM, a holistic framework for evaluating language models across accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency, providing comprehensive multi-metric benchmarking.

papers.title: Aligning AI With Shared Human Values
papers.authors: Hendrycks, D., Burns, C., Basart, S., Critch, A., Li, J., Song, D., & Steinhardt, J.
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces the ETHICS benchmark for evaluating LLMs on justice, deontology, virtue ethics, utilitarianism, and commonsense morality, establishing a multi-framework approach to moral evaluation.

papers.title: MoralBench: Moral Evaluation of LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes MoralBench for evaluating the moral reasoning capabilities of LLMs across diverse ethical scenarios, providing fine-grained analysis of model strengths and weaknesses.

papers.title: LLM Ethics Benchmark: Three-Dimensional Assessment of Moral Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a three-dimensional framework for evaluating LLM ethical reasoning covering moral recognition, moral judgment, and moral action, with empirical evaluation across multiple LLMs.

papers.title: A roadmap for evaluating moral competence in large language models
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a comprehensive roadmap for evaluating moral competence in LLMs, arguing that current benchmarks are insufficient and outlining key dimensions for assessment.

papers.title: Beyond Verdicts: Evaluating Language Model Moral Competence
papers.abstract_snippet: Argues that evaluating LLM moral competence requires going beyond simple verdict accuracy to assess reasoning quality, consistency, and sensitivity to morally relevant features.

papers.title: Can Machines Learn Morality? The Delphi Experiment and the Limits of AI
papers.abstract_snippet: Critically examines the Delphi moral reasoning system and broader attempts to teach machines morality, arguing that fundamental limitations in current approaches constrain moral AI.

papers.title: Evaluating the Moral Beliefs Encoded in LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Develops methods to probe and evaluate the moral beliefs encoded within LLMs, revealing systematic patterns in how models represent and reason about ethical questions.

papers.title: MoReBench: A Comprehensive Moral Reasoning Benchmark for LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces MoReBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating moral reasoning in LLMs across multiple ethical frameworks and cultural contexts, with fine-grained evaluation metrics.

papers.title: Decoding Moral Responses in AI
papers.abstract_snippet: Analyzes how AI systems decode and generate moral responses, examining the alignment between model outputs and human moral intuitions across different ethical frameworks.
